newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Electric offers portion of savings.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Electric offers portion of savings.

text.p: Atlantic Energy Inc said the one percent rate reduction Atlantic Electric offered as a result of the company's proposed merger with Delmarva Power & Light Co represents one-third of the synergy savings expected from the merger.

In a statement to members of the financial community providing additional details on Atlantic Electric's filing with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, the company also said it purchases 579 megawatts of power from NUGs -- non-utility generators.
It went on to say the utility's estimate of $965 million of stranded costs associated with those contracts is based on contract terms which run for an additional 18 to 27 years.
These contracts represent about 24 percent of the company's annual revenues, it said, adding the contracts had an average cost of $0.107 per kilowatthour in 1996.

The statement also detailed the company's estimates, developed using an internal market price forecast, that stranded costs for its owned generation capacity totals $341 million. (Its table is reproduced at the end of this item.)

Atlantic Energy said the utility has proposed a $7.2 million annual rate reduction upon completion of the proposed merger with Delmarva Power, noting this is expected to be completed around year end 1997.
"This amount represents one third of the synergy savings from the merger" and will be available upon regulatory approval of the pending merger request, it said.
The additional projected revenue reduction of about $40 million a year, beginning in 2001, is related to reductions in operating costs.
This includes amounts currently being collected and amortized for changes in state tax law and for utility purchased power agreements, which amortizations expire in 2000, it explained.

It said the board plans to transfer the stranded cost and unbundled rate portions of the filings for all four New Jersey electric utilities to the Office of Administrative Law for evidentiary hearings and initial decision by April 1998. The board has retained the review of each company's restructuring plans, with the overall objective being full reviews completed by October 1998, Atlantic Energy said.
The other three utilities operating in New Jersey are GPU Inc, Public Service Enterprise Group Inc and Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc.

(A) Assumes net cash flows (expected market revenues less operating expenses or purchase power payments) through remaining life of asset or contract term discounted at 9.76 percent. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
